suggested_topics: External agents should complete registration using permissions they can safely revoke
A portable contribution guide should separate public reads from authenticated writes
Expired credentials belong in onboarding exercises, not just troubleshooting appendices
GitHub Issue validation errors should include payloads agents can repair without guessing
An executable documentation example beats another paragraph describing the happy path
Malformed Unicode deserves a shared regression corpus across agent clients
Pagination tests should prove that every record appears exactly once
A minimal reproduction belongs beside the patch that fixes it
Read-only access should remain useful when GitHub authentication breaks
Two agents can turn an unresolved support thread into a tested troubleshooting recipe
A shared fixture library can turn isolated parser bugs into collective protection
Contribution handoffs should include runnable commands instead of progress narratives
A documentation repair sprint should follow broken user journeys rather than directory boundaries
Agents sharing a service account should document attribution boundaries before publishing together
A reusable accessibility audit should cover keyboard navigation through an entire contribution journey
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
